disclosures_before_this_commit: Stage A replay and comparison-unit audit (c54_audit.py replay / unit) were run on the stored WL53 data before this protocol was written. Observed: the stored G3 groups replay to 0.0 difference; V0 (WL53 interior unit) and V1 (centre-ray unit) agree exactly on every face-on camera and differ by up to 8-33 percentage points on the 10-port oblique side-face groups (e.g. gap4 obot slab_lo:-y +2.1 % vs -31.5 %, gap8 obot slab_lo:-y -24.5 % vs -16.2 %)

Exploratory Lambert runs (explore1-3, no Cycles reference) were made on gap4 (levels 2..32) and floor_lam (levels 2,4,8) to check feasibility and cost. Observed before the protocol: for floor_lam dom:bot the Galerkin-coarse vs fine-projection difference was +6.14 % and the production sampler vs exact Galerkin -0.08 %; for gap4 the fine solution converges geometrically in the uniform refinement level (successive pooled changes on the gap faces 7.1 / 1.3 / 0.45 / 0.15 % for s = 2 -> 4 -> 8 -> 16 -> 32) and the coarse interface is +20 % / +44 % off on slab_lo:top / slab_hi:bot. The refinement criterion constants below (c = 2, l_max = 8) were declared from the Galerkin error scaling (w / d)^2, not tuned on these runs; the sensitivity arms c = 1 and c = 4 are reported next to the primary and none of the arms is selected after results

A fixed-seed observation: WL53's ray-count control (128 / 512 / 2048 C rays per out-cell) reused the same sun-visibility realization (K_ext = 256, seed 5341) in every variant, so it does not bound the noise of that estimator; this protocol therefore runs replicate seeds and one-factor variants

conventions.units: as WL53 (m; radiance W m^-2 sr^-1; flux W; sun = collimated beam with perpendicular irradiance E = 1)
conventions.K_lambert: opaque Lambert, rho = 0.8 grey, exact local K at every spatial resolution (no directional dependence: out-bin and in-bin counts do not change a Lambert result)
conventions.C: p53_compose.cast_C unchanged: unbiased ray estimator of the flux fraction leaving an out-cell whose air ray first enters an in-cell; uniform position on the cell, uniform in projected solid angle inside the out-bin
conventions.coarse_ports: WL53 1 cm ports (production C0 interface). Fine unknown = one cell of an s x s subdivision of a port (s = 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32); cell flux is a conservative partition of the port flux (area weights)
conventions.projection: coarse radiance of a port = area-weighted mean of the fine cell radiances (conservative: coarse flux = sum of fine flux)
conventions.galerkin: C_g[I, J] = sum_{i in I, j in J} C_ij A_j / A_J: the exact operator for a piecewise-constant coarse field (uniform radiance per port)
conventions.comparison_unit_primary: V1: port average over every pixel whose CENTRE ray hits the port (the Cycles image is point-sampled), >= 30 pixels per port; WL53's interior unit V0 (centre and four corner rays) is reported next to it for every group. Primary because the image is point-sampled and V1 is unbiased for a point-sampled field; V0 drops edge rows
conventions.bias: B = sum(pred - ref) / sum(ref) over the ports of a group (WL53 definition); a group is ruled if it has >= 5 ports and >= 2 % of the camera's reference signal; 3 % rule: |B| <= 0.03 + 3 SE (SE from the reference seeds, plus replicate seeds where used)
conventions.ruled_group_labels: component:face (as WL53 port_groups); floor is one group
conventions.nonfinite: metrics JSON replaces nonfinite numbers by null (c54_common.dump uses allow_nan = False)

fixtures_lambert.cycles_reference: Cycles 3.5.1, Lambert, seeds 5401-5404, 2048 spp, 0.5 mm pixels (1 mm for top / otop), WL53 reset() settings (point-sampled Gaussian 0.01 px, 1024 bounces, no clamping, sun angle 0); the WL53 Lambert chain control (1.0000003) and direct-lit faces (<= 0.5 %) validate the renderer's radiometry for these materials

decomposition.A_representation: G_sref vs F_sref (exact transfer integrals on the coarse interface vs the converged fine solution projected onto it): the error of the piecewise-constant 1 cm interface
decomposition.B_sampled_C: C0prod vs G_sref and the replicate / one-factor arms: production sampler and sun-visibility estimator on that interface

stage_B.reference_level: sref = 16 for every fixture. Convergence rule: the pooled change of every ruled group between s = 8 and s = 16 is <= 1 %; otherwise the group is flagged unconverged and |F16 - F8| is reported as its reference uncertainty. gap4 s = 32 is the convergence check of s = 16
stage_B.source_receiver_separation: known-field transfer test: with the converged fine outgoing flux phi_F as the prescribed source field, the receiver port irradiance with the fine source (exact) vs with the source averaged per coarse port (uniform radiance per port) -> the source-averaging effect; split by source-receiver distance bins (< h, h-2h, 2h-4h, > 4h); plus synthetic prescribed fields (uniform, linear ramp, exponential decay, step). Receiver averaging is lossless for port flux by construction (conservative sum) and is reported as such; its only consequence is the uniform re-emission assumption at the next bounce, which is the same source-averaging assumption

attribution_rules.spatial: For every ruled group that misses the 3 % rule in T (C0prod vs Cycles V1) on a face-on camera: attribution fraction a = A / (C0prod vs F_sref bias). Spatial attribution of the group: SUPPORTED if 0.5 <= a <= 1.5 and |B (replicate mean)| <= 1 %; estimator noise if replicate sd >= 0.5 |T bias|; comparison unit if |V1 - V0| >= 0.5 |T bias|; readout / reference if |F_sref vs Cycles V1| >= 0.5 |T bias|. Factors that satisfy none are reported as unattributed
attribution_rules.overall: SPATIAL ATTRIBUTION is SUPPORTED if the Lambert control floor_lam (dom:bot and floor under the box, camera underup / underdown) and the Lambert gap4 / gap8 gap faces are each spatially attributed; PARTIAL if some are; NOT SUPPORTED otherwise

candidate_CASP.name: contact-adaptive sub-port explicit coupling (CASP)
candidate_CASP.description: ONE mechanism: conservative adaptive refinement of the explicit C unknowns (hierarchical-radiosity-style link refinement). A port is subdivided into l x l cells (one unknown per cell) where its near-field transport is spatially resolved only by cells smaller than the distance to the surfaces it exchanges light with. The criterion is geometry only (independent of lighting and of the radiance field), so it is recomputed with C when geometry changes
candidate_CASP.level_rule: per port J: cast 256 cosine-weighted rays (seed 5801) from uniform positions; nu(J) = fraction of rays with first-hit distance t < 4 h (h = 1 cm); if nu(J) < 0.05 then l(J) = 1 else d(J) = median of the t < 4 h hits and l(J) = clamp(2^ceil(log2(c h / d(J))), 1, l_max). Primary c = 2, l_max = 8; sensitivity arms c = 1 and c = 4 (l_max 8) are reported, none selected
candidate_CASP.unknowns: cells (port, a, b) of the l x l subdivision, built from the port's current grid (bilinear in the port's 4 / 2 grid points; rigid and non-rigid deformations carry through the coarse-port grid)
candidate_CASP.rays_budget: equal to production: rays per coarse port = 128 x 64 = 8192; cells of an l x l port get 8192 / l^2 rays each (>= 32); reported also with 4x budget as a sensitivity arm
candidate_CASP.conservative_mapping: sources: coarse flux -> cell flux by area weights; receivers: cell flux -> coarse port flux by sum. A domain whose K is port-resolved (WL53 medium TR operator, K_coarse) stays at coarse unknowns: its receiving cells collapse by sum and its emission is uniform per (port, out-bin); the refinement therefore acts on domains with local K (Lambert / opaque) and on the K-C interface through receiver sums. K's coefficients and meaning are unchanged. A medium-to-medium link is unchanged in expectation: this is a predeclared architectural dependency, tested in Stage E (including a labelled matched-resolution oracle control with TR at 5 mm ports, Dout = Din = 16)
candidate_CASP.preserved: positivity (rays carry non-negative weights), flux closure (every ray hits a cell or escapes), path ownership (air segments only; no medium sub-path), source / receiver direction semantics (bins in the parent port frame), reciprocity of the area-weighted flux

stage_D_tests.analytic_form_factor: coaxial parallel squares (10 cm side, gaps 4 / 8 / 30 mm; Modest / Hottel closed form) vs the C estimate at s = 8, 16 and CASP: <= 1 % (MC noise accounted)
stage_D_tests.flux_closure: sum of a column of C plus escape = 1 to 1e-6 for every cell, every arm (CASP incl.)
stage_D_tests.reciprocity: area-weighted: A_i F_(i<-j) vs A_j F_(j<-i) pooled asymmetry <= 1.25 x the cross-seed statistic + 0.005 (WL53 rule), for uniform s and for CASP's mixed-level mesh
stage_D_tests.zero_and_superposition: zero source gives exactly 0; solve(a + b) = solve(a) + solve(b) to 1e-6 relative (linear operator)
stage_D_tests.escape_accounting: escape fraction per cell + sum of C column = 1; open geometry (floor) escapes counted
stage_D_tests.blocker: no C entry across an opaque blocker: a thin black plate between two plates removes the transfer (< 1e-9) in uniform s and CASP
stage_D_tests.rigid_consistency: rotating + translating a whole scene leaves the pooled port radiance unchanged to the MC noise (cross-seed statistic); CASP levels are rotation-invariant
stage_D_tests.same_domain_reentry: concave L-block exposed self-interreflection preserved with the same flux as the fine uniform solution within MC noise; convex box has none
stage_D_tests.no_path_duplication_with_K: medium domains: zero back-face hits in cast_C (rays that would enter a medium never start in air); Lambert / medium arms keep K as the only in-domain operator (no refined cell carries a medium sub-path); the WL53 'dup' control semantics are not re-opened
stage_D_tests.determinism: the same seed gives the same C and radiance bit for bit; chunk size does not change the solution beyond 1e-6 (float64 accumulation in the solver)
stage_D_tests.k_c_fixed_point: the coupled solve converges (rho < 1, closure <= 1) and an iteration-count independent solution is reached to 1e-7 relative change; rho reported
stage_D_tests.wl53_regression: experiments/phys_ref53/tests/test_p53.py (9 tests) is re-run unchanged on LabServer69; shared WL53 code is not modified

arms.Cfine: uniform fine explicit transport oracle (diagnostic ceiling, s = 8 for Lambert)
arms.Kfine_control: labelled matched-resolution control: TR slab operator at 5 mm ports (Dout = Din = 16) with uniform fine C (s = 2), against the matched coarse (1 cm, Dout = Din = 16) operator; run only if the coarse-K arms leave medium-to-medium groups unresolved

stage_E.scenes: Lambert: gap4, gap8, gap30, floor_lam, lblock_lam, rot_lam. WL53 medium K (stored T matrices, coarse K): gap4, gap8, floor (slab over Lambert floor), lblock, and bend90 / dent with stale (rest) and current K if the interface supports it
stage_E.metrics: incoming transport accuracy (single-flight known-field transfer), single-flight transfer error vs the fine solve, coupled error vs Cycles (V1 primary, V0 reported) per group / camera / channel, multi-bounce rho and closure, near-contact bias (ports with nu >= 0.05), visibility-boundary bias (rot_lam), oblique-side groups (reported separately, always including gap8 obot slab_lo:-y), temporal change tracking (T0 -> T1 by the rigid box move in rot_lam vs floor_lam and by bend90 / dent), per-material / per-face error, full per-port error distribution (p50 / p90 / p99 / max)
stage_E.composition_restoration: RESTORED only if every ruled group of every required fixture passes the historical 3 % rule (|B| <= 0.03 + 3 SE, V1 primary) in all three channels. A candidate that reduces the worst ruled |B| by >= 50 % but misses is PARTIAL evidence
stage_E.differential_K_update: paired differential D = pred(stale K) - pred(current K) with the same C and the same reference: the reference cancels in err_stale - err_current. Ranking stale vs current is reliable on a group iff |D_g| > 2 (|B_current,g| + 3 SE_g) (a shared bias smaller than |D| / 2 cannot flip the order), with SE_D from the TR seed pair; a separate 1 % differential-error target is evaluated as |D_g - D_g(fine C)| <= 0.01 of the group signal; the 3 % absolute rule is not replaced by it

evidence_classes.attribution_evidence: Stage B decomposition and the source / receiver separation; descriptive, rules above
evidence_classes.operator_correctness: Stage D tests all pass for C1 (uniform fine and CASP)
evidence_classes.composition_restoration: Stage E, Lambert exact-K fixtures: RESTORED per the rule above; medium-K scenes reported separately and never pooled with Lambert
evidence_classes.efficient_candidate_viability: RESTORED (Lambert) AND unknowns <= 4 x the coarse unknowns AND C build + 20 solve iterations <= 10 x the same quantity for C0 on the same GPU, uncontended, 5 repeats, CUDA-synchronised; otherwise the candidate is a high-accuracy diagnostic C only. Production real-time readiness is a separate milestone and is not claimed from any of these
evidence_classes.scalability: empirical timings vs port count (floor 10 / 20 / 30 / 60 cm), near-contact density (gap 4 / 8 / 30 mm) and a geometry change (box shift); no asymptotic claim without an algorithmic argument and measurements

stage_F_cost: per arm: level-assignment prepass, relation (C) build, sun term, solve iterations, application (sparse mm), end-to-end update after a rigid box move, peak GPU memory (torch.cuda.max_memory_allocated after reset), nnz and bytes of C, CPU / GPU split; hardware matched, uncontended; the historical Python-looped relation build is not used as the comparison when the GPU caster (cast_C with chunking) is the apples-to-apples C0

verdict_mapping.baseline_audit_reliability: SUPPORTED if the stored WL53 composition tables replay exactly, the fresh composition reproduces the stored predictions to the determinism tolerance, and the discrepancies found in the WL53 prose are listed; CONDITIONALLY SUPPORTED if tables reproduce but claims A-E carry a listed caveat
verdict_mapping.candidate_physical_correctness: SUPPORTED if every Stage D test passes
verdict_mapping.absolute_composition_accuracy: SUPPORTED if RESTORED on all Lambert fixtures and on the medium-K scenes with a coarse-K-compatible interface; CONDITIONALLY SUPPORTED if RESTORED on the Lambert fixtures only; NOT SUPPORTED otherwise
verdict_mapping.near_contact_oblique_fidelity: per the near-contact / oblique-group metrics; the oblique 10-port side groups are judged on V1 and V0 together and are never excluded
verdict_mapping.production_integration_readiness: NOT SUPPORTED unless every item above is SUPPORTED and the K-C interface dependency is resolved; not expected from this batch

amendments.type: POST HOC (labelled): comparison-coverage rule and reference pixel-size diagnostic. The declared rules, thresholds and verdict mapping are NOT changed; every table is reported under the declared rule AND the amended rule
observed_before_this_amendment: Stage B primary (gap4, gap8, gap30, floor_lam; Cycles seeds 5401-5404) was computed and read. floor_lam underup dom:bot: C0 vs Cycles +6.2 %, A (Galerkin coarse vs fine) +6.2 %, F16 vs Cycles -0.0 %. floor_lam underdown floor: C0 vs Cycles +4.3 % but C0 vs F16 +1.1 % and F16 vs Cycles +3.1 %; the pixel-pooled fine-vs-Cycles bias is -0.6 % and the radial profile of the ratio is flat to 1-2 %

A coverage sensitivity (c54_coverage.py) showed the floor-under-box group falls to C0 +1.2 % / F16 -0.8 % when only fully covered ports (>= 90 % of the port's expected pixel count, n = 144 of 196) are kept; the declared '>= 30 pixels' rule was copied from WL53 where a port had ~100 pixels (1 mm), whereas 0.5 mm pixels give ~400, so 30 pixels is 7.5 % of a port

gap4 gapdown slab_lo:top (100 fully visible ports): F16 vs Cycles -5.2 % although the fine solution is converged (0.15 % between s = 16 and 32) and the same fine solution matches Cycles on gapup slab_hi:bot (-0.2 %)

the 10-port obot groups of the gap scenes are seen through the gap: a 50 deg line of sight enters a gap of height g only g tan 50 deg deep (4.8 mm for gap4), so the reference port average covers only the open-edge part of a 10 mm port while every prediction is a full-port average
amendments.amended_comparison_rule: expected-coverage rule (geometry only, no image look): a port enters the AMENDED ruled set only if pixels(port) >= 0.9 x expected, expected = (sum over the port's triangles of area x max(0, n . c)) / pixel_area, c = unit vector to the camera. Ports with 30 <= pixels < 0.9 x expected are 'partially visible': they stay in the DECLARED tables, are listed separately in the amended tables with their coverage, and are evaluated at pixel level through the fine solution (c54_stageB pixelwise) instead of by a port average. Nothing is dropped from the reports
amendments.diagnostic: gap4 cameras gapdown and gapup re-rendered with Cycles at pixel sizes 0.5, 0.25, 0.125 mm (one seed 5499, 2048 spp, otherwise the declared reference settings) into out/cycles_res
amendments.interpretation_rule_fixed_now: a group whose F16-vs-Cycles bias at 0.5 mm exceeds 3 % is attributed to REFERENCE POINT-SAMPLING (aliasing of a sharp sun / shadow edge) if the Cycles port average moves toward F16 as the pixel shrinks: |F16 - Cycles(0.125 mm)| <= 0.5 |F16 - Cycles(0.5 mm)|; otherwise the discrepancy stays UNATTRIBUTED and the group's reference is reported as not validated at that tolerance
amendments.consequence_for_verdicts: composition-restoration is evaluated on the amended ruled set against the Cycles reference ONLY for groups whose F16-vs-Cycles agreement is within 3 % + 3 SE (validated reference groups); groups where the fine reference and Cycles disagree by more than that are reported with both references and are not counted as pass or fail of C1 against Cycles; C1 is then judged against the fine reference F16 for them (labelled as such)

amendments.type: POST HOC (labelled): audit finding on the spectral-radius estimator; implementation correction of MY metric (no rule, threshold or verdict-mapping change)
amendments.observed: Stage E first run (preserved in out/stageE_v1_wl53rho): the floor scene (WL53 slab over a Lambert floor) reported rho(R) = 0.7244 (C0, equal to WL53's stored value), 0.3866 (CASP) and 0.1795 (uniform s = 4) from p53_compose.spectral_radius, although all arms converged in the same 38 iterations to the same totals (slab R flux 21.86 / 21.99, floor 104.38 / 104.48) and one K-C step transfers identical fluxes (floor to slab 0.1294-0.1295, slab to floor 0.4852). scipy Arnoldi on the matrix-free K C operator gives top |lambda| = 0.7292 / 0.7318 / 0.7324 (s = 1 / 2 / 4), each as a +- pair (bipartite slab <-> floor exchange)
amendments.diagnosis: p53_compose.spectral_radius iterates A and reports the last norm ratio; with a +- pair the iterate alternates between two modes and the ratio is not |lambda_1|. It is not a valid estimator for bipartite couplings; it was within 1 % for the coarse floor scene by luck and under-reports refined operators by 2-4x. The WL53 values of rho (gap4 0.816 / 0.738 / 0.452, ...) used this estimator; WL53's convergence statements (iterations, residual 1e-7) do not depend on it
amendments.change: c54_casp.rho_robust: power iteration on A^2 from a positive start, sqrt of the flux-sum ratio. Every WL54 arm reports rho (robust) and rho_wl53_power300 side by side. Validation rule fixed now: the robust estimator is accepted if it matches the Arnoldi top |lambda| within 2 % in every case of c54_rho_check.py (floor and gap4, s = 1 and 2); otherwise rho is reported as the Arnoldi value only
amendments.consequence: Stage E was re-run with the robust estimator (same seeds, same predictions); the K control (c54_kfine.py) was launched before the correction and reports only the WL53 estimator: its rho values are not used
